diagnostic_evidence.quote: D_{j,j\pm 1}^{x}= \frac{\pm 1}{2\Delta x}\;,\qquad D_{j,j}^{xx}= - \frac{2}{\left(\Delta x\right)^2}\;, \quad D_{j,j\pm 1}^{xx}= \frac{1}{\left(\Delta x\right)^2}\;,

issues.failure_explanation: The stated boundary modifications zero entries in rows 1 and N_x (e.g. D^x_{1,2}=0) while leaving the transposed entries untouched (D^x_{2,1}=-1/(2Δx)). Hence D^x is not antisymmetric (D^x_{2,1}≠−D^x_{1,2}) and D^{xx} is not symmetric (D^{xx}_{2,1}=1/(Δx)²≠0=D^{xx}_{1,2}), so all three summation-by-parts identities fail. True periodic wrap-around entries (D^x_{1,N_x}=−1/(2Δx), D^x_{N_x,1}=+1/(2Δx), D^{xx}_{1,N_x}=D^{xx}_{N_x,1}=1/(Δx)²) are never added, so the matrices are not circulant and the Fourier diagonalisation in lemma:fullydiscreteCFL (eigenvalues λ^x_α=i sin ν_α/Δx etc.) does not apply to them.

failure_location.quote: \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} y_j D_{ji}^x z_i = - \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{x} y_i\;, \qquad \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{x} z_i = 0 \;, \qquad \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} y_j D_{ji}^{xx} z_i = \sum_{i,j=1}^{N_x} z_j D_{ji}^{xx} y_i.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the boundary zeroing with standard periodic wrap-around stencil entries so that D^x is antisymmetric circulant, D^{xx} is symmetric circulant, and D^+ is the periodic forward difference; the lemma properties and the Fourier analysis then hold with no further changes.
issues.overall_effect: Every stability proof that invokes the summation-by-parts identities or the Fourier/CFL estimate—full-system stability (theorem:stabilityMg) and DLRA stability (thm:added-1)—becomes unsupported as written.
issues.title: Boundary-modified stencil matrices fail summation-by-parts and Fourier diagonalization
issues.why_classification: Fixing a few boundary stencil entries (local, routine) restores every claimed property and all downstream proofs, with no loss of any claim, rate, or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for $g_{jk}^n = 1$ the condition $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} g_{jk}^n \omega_k e^{v_k^2/2} = 1$ holds

issues.failure_explanation: Standard Gauss–Hermite quadrature with weight e^{−v²} is exact only for polynomials of degree ≤ 2N_v−1. The asserted identity (1/√(2π))Σ_k ω_k e^{v_k²/2}=1 is the quadrature approximation of (1/√(2π))∫e^{−v²/2}dv=1 with non-polynomial integrand e^{v²/2}, so it is not exact. The proof of lemma:fullydiscrete-rho inserts this identity as an equality, so the discrete mass-conservation claim Σ_k f^n_{jk}ω_k e^{v_k²}=ρ^n_j holds only up to quadrature error. The same identity is used again in the collision-term simplification of theorem:stabilityMg and thm:added-1.

failure_location.quote: We insert the induction assumption as well as $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \sum_{k=1}^{N_v} \omega_k e^{v_k^2/2} = 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt a quadrature rule exact for the weight e^{−v²/2} (rescaled Gauss–Hermite) so that Σ_k ω_k = √(2π) holds exactly and adjust the e^{v_k²/2} factors consistently, or weaken every exact conservation/stability statement to hold up to a controlled quadrature-error remainder.
issues.overall_effect: Exact discrete mass conservation (lemma:fullydiscrete-rho) and both exact H-norm stability guarantees (theorem:stabilityMg, thm:added-1) hold only approximately, to quadrature accuracy, rather than exactly as stated.
issues.title: Gauss-Hermite quadrature identity used as exact in conservation lemma is only approximate
issues.why_classification: Replacing the quadrature rule and re-deriving the discretisation, or weakening exact conservation and stability to approximate ones, requires a contained but non-trivial construction beyond a local edit; however no global proof architecture is lost and the method, scope, and rate survive recognisably.

issues.failure_explanation: The augmentation gives span(Ẍ)=span(X̂)+span((ρ^{n+1})²X̂). The claimed identity P^X((ρ^{n+1})²⊙g^{n+1}_{·β})=(ρ^{n+1})²⊙g^{n+1}_{·β} requires (ρ^{n+1})²⊙v to lie in span(Ẍ) for every v∈span(Ẍ). Writing v=u+(ρ^{n+1})²⊙w with u,w∈span(X̂) yields (ρ^{n+1})²⊙v=(ρ^{n+1})²⊙u+(ρ^{n+1})⁴⊙w. The second summand lies in span((ρ^{n+1})⁴X̂), which is not contained in span(Ẍ) in general. Because the S-step evolves in the full augmented space Ẍ⊗V̈, its output g^{n+1} generically has components in the augmented directions, so the projection identity is false. The velocity identity fails identically: (ωe^{v²/2})⊙v for v=u+(ωe^{v²/2})⊙w introduces ω²e^{v²}⊙w outside span(V̈).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish stability of the DLRA scheme without the false projection identities, e.g. by restricting the S-step output to span(X̂)⊗span(V̂) (which would require a modified algorithm) or by constructing an alternative stability argument that bounds the projected update without Hadamard-product invariance.
issues.overall_effect: The H-norm stability guarantee for the DLRA scheme (Theorem thm:added-1) is unproved; the entire derivation from the projected S-step to the norm inequality rests on a false identity. Finite further augmentations do not close the gap because each new layer introduces (ρ^{n+1})^{2m} (or ω^m e^{mv²/2}) directions.
issues.title: DLRA stability proof relies on projection identities not guaranteed by basis augmentation
issues.why_classification: The key identity is provably false for the stated augmentation; no finite augmentation scheme closes the Hadamard-product gap, and no alternative proof or algorithmic fix preserving the advertised stability guarantee is supported by the source. Every supported resolution requires essentially new proof architecture or loses the DLRA stability guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The last step consists in truncating the augmented quantities $\doublehat{\mathbf{X}}^{n+1}$, $\doublehat{\mathbf{V}}^{n+1}$ and $\doublehat{\mathbf{S}}^{n+1}$ from rank $4r$ to a new rank $r_1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stability inequality is derived for the pre-truncation S-step output g^{n+1}=ẌŜ^{n+1}V̈^⊤. The modified truncation replaces Ŝ^{n+1} by a rank-reduced S^{n+1}, producing a different matrix and hence a different ‖f^{n+1}‖²_H. Truncation is performed via the SVD of the coupling matrix in the standard Frobenius norm, which does not control the weighted H-norm (whose weights involve ρ_j² and ω_k e^{v_k²/2}). The claim that truncation 'is designed not to alter these expressions' is justified only for the mass-conservation identity (H₂Z=0 is preserved because Z is orthogonal to all nonzero right singular vectors of H₂), not for the H-norm monotonicity ‖f^{n+1}_trunc‖²_H ≤ ‖f^{n+1}_pre‖²_H, which is never established.

failure_location.quote: Analogously to the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem:stabilityMg} and, as the truncation step is designed not to alter these expressions, we can conclude that the proposed DLRA scheme is numerically stable under the time step restriction $\max_k(|v_k|) \Delta t \leq \Delta x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide an argument showing that the modified truncation preserves or decreases the H-norm (for instance by truncating in the H-weighted norm rather than the Frobenius norm of Ŝ), or restructure the stability proof to bound the truncated output directly.
issues.overall_effect: Even if the derivation of the pre-truncation stability inequality were repaired (ISSUE-003), H-norm monotonicity for the actual output of the DLRA scheme (after truncation) would remain unestablished, leaving Theorem thm:added-1 unproved for the algorithm as stated.
issues.title: Truncation step's effect on H-norm stability inequality is unjustified
issues.why_classification: A contained non-trivial argument or a modified truncation criterion (weighted SVD) can close the gap while preserving the advertised stability guarantee and the mass-conservation design; no global proof architecture change is required.
